questions: Did the unsteady walking begin suddenly, within the last 24 hours?
Do you have new weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Do you have trouble speaking, understanding speech, swallowing, or controlling your face?
Do you have double vision or sudden loss of vision?
Do you have a severe or unusual headache?
Do you have spinning dizziness or a sensation that the room is moving?
Have you recently fallen or hit your head?
Are you currently confused, unusually sleepy, or difficult to wake?
Have you recently consumed a large amount of alcohol or taken recreational drugs?
Have you started, stopped, or had a dose increase of any medication recently?
Do you have fever, neck stiffness, or a recent serious infection?
Is the unsteadiness worse when your eyes are closed or in the dark?
Do you have numbness or reduced ability to feel your feet?
Do you have shaking, clumsiness of your hands, or difficulty reaching accurately for objects?
Do you have trouble coordinating your speech or speaking as clearly as usual?
Have you had vomiting or severe nausea along with the unsteadiness?
Has this problem been present for more than one month?
Has the unsteadiness been gradually worsening?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Do you have a history of stroke, multiple sclerosis, seizures, migraine, or other neurological disease?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, vitamin B12 deficiency, or liver disease?
Do you have a history of heavy or prolonged alcohol use?
Does anyone in your family have a similar walking problem or an inherited neurological condition?
Are you unable to walk without support?

results: 1. Full neurological examination, including ocular pursuit and saccades, nystagmus, dysarthria assessment, finger–nose and heel–shin testing, rapid alternating movements, tandem gait, Romberg test, and reflexes
gait examination: wide-based, unsteady gait
finger-nose / heel-shin testing: dysmetria
Romberg test: negative - swaying is not worse with the eyes closed
bedside eye-movement exam: no ophthalmoplegia and no nystagmus - the classic triad is incomplete
cranial nerve examination: normal
mental status / cognitive screen: MMSE 23/30
muscle tone examination: normal
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
fundoscopy: normal
2. MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium, including diffusion-weighted imaging
brain MRI: bilateral symmetric hyperintensity in the mammillary bodies, thalami and periaqueductal midbrain, with the LENTIFORM FORK SIGN; reversed after treatment
MRI brain with gadolinium: abnormal; bilateral symmetric mammillary body, thalamic and periaqueductal midbrain hyperintensities with lentiform fork sign
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: abnormal; bilateral symmetric restricted diffusion in the mammillary bodies, thalami and periaqueductal midbrain
3. Complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function, liver function, calcium, magnesium, glucose, and thyroid-stimulating hormone
full blood count: normal
renal and liver function: end-stage renal disease on maintenance haemodialysis
electrolytes (Na, K, Ca, Mg): normal
glucose / HbA1c: HbA1c 5.9% (reference 4.0-6.0) - normal
TSH / free T4: normal
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: abnormal; end-stage renal failure with elevated urea and creatinine
liver function tests: normal
serum calcium, magnesium and phosphate: normal
blood glucose and HbA1c: normal; HbA1c 5.9%
4. Serum vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, folate, and vitamin E
vitamin B12 / folate: normal
vitamin E: normal
vitamin B12 with methylmalonic acid: normal
serum folate: normal
5. Serum copper and ceruloplasmin
copper / caeruloplasmin: normal - excludes Wilson disease
6. Lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal-fluid cell count, protein, glucose, oligoclonal bands, IgG index, and infectious studies
lumbar puncture / CSF: normal cells, protein and glucose; no oligoclonal bands
CSF cell count and differential: normal
CSF protein: normal
CSF glucose: normal
CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index: normal
CSF culture and viral PCR: normal
7. Electroencephalogram
EEG: normal
8. MRI of the cervical and thoracic spinal cord with and without gadolinium
MRI cervical and thoracic spine: normal
9. Serum anti-GAD65, anti-Yo, anti-Hu, anti-Ri, and other paraneoplastic neurological antibodies
paraneoplastic antibody panel (serum): negative
anti-GAD antibodies: negative
10. Genetic testing for episodic ataxia and hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia panels
genetic ataxia panel: no pathogenic repeat expansion or variant
